newsitem.title: USA: "The Life", musical about hookers, tops Tonys list. [CORRECTED 00:30 GMT 6/5]
newsitem.headline: "The Life", musical about hookers, tops Tonys list. [CORRECTED 00:30 GMT 6/5]

text.p: "The Life," a Cy Coleman musical about Times Square prostitutes, topped the list of Broadway's Tony Awards with 12 nominations on Monday, including the coveted best musical.

Close behind was John Kander and Fred Ebb's (corrects from Fred Kander and John Ebb) "Steel Pier," the Depression-era dance marathon show that won 11 nominations including best musical, best book, best score, best direction and nods for its leads, Karen Ziemba and Daniel McDonald.

"Titanic," at $10 million the season's most expensive show, managed only five nominations but was among the best musical, book and score nominees, unlike "Jekyll and Hyde," another expensive and much-hyped musical.

That show toured extensively before opening on Broadway and has somewhat of a cult following, but was passed over for best musical and score. It did garner nominations for Robert Cuccioli in the title role, best book, costumes and lighting.
Instead "Juan Darien, A Carnival Mass", a small, long- closed fable that used puppets, rounded out the best musical category. That show tied with "Titanic" in total nominations.

On the drama side, best play nominees included David Hare's "Skylight," a British import about a reunion of ex-lovers played by Michael Gambon and Lia Williams, who were nominated for best actor and best actress.

Pam Gems' "Stanley," about British artist Stanley Spencer, "The Last Night of Ballyhoo," Alfred Uhry's comic drama about assimilationist U.S. Southern Jews in 1939, and Horton Foote's "The Young Man From Atlanta," about a 1950s couple coping with their son's death, were the other best play nominees. "Atlanta" also won a nomination for Shirley Knight.
Broadway's season ended last week with a slew of openings, most to tepid reviews, making the 12 citations for "The Life", a sort of "Sweet Charity" for the 90s, especially impressive.

Coleman, who also wrote "Sweet Charity," was nominated for the score, and the show also took nods for lead actress Pamela Isaacs, book, direction, choreography, costumes, lighting, orchestrations and for three of its featured performers.

Best musical revival nominees were "Chicago," with a total of eight nominations, "Candide," whose star Jim Dale was cited for best actor, "Annie" and "Once Upon a Mattress." Bebe Neuwirth and James Naughton were both nominated for "Chicago."

Best play revival nods went to the London import "A Doll's House," which also won a best actress in a play nomination for Janet McTeer, Noel Coward's "Present Laughter," "The Gin Game" which also won a nomination for star Julie Harris, and "London Assurance," whose star Brian Bedford was cited for best actor.

Other best play actor nominees were Christopher Plummer in the one-man show "Barrymore" and Anthony Sher in "Stanley." "Play On," a Duke Ellington musical, brought Tonya Pinkins a best actress nomination.
The 51st annual Tonys will be presented on June 1.
